findings.source_quote: so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt ... Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death
findings.suggested_fix: State that these are English words beginning with D, and retain each English headword with its Greek meaning. Include all fourteen entries, distinguishing Disappointment (απογοήτευση), Disillusionment (διάψευση προσδοκιών), Despondency (αποκαρδίωση), and Despair (απελπισία). Do not claim that the Greek equivalents begin with Δ.
findings.translation_quote: αρχίζουν με το γράμμα Δ: Απογοήτευση, Δισταγμός ... Απελπισία, Κατάθλιψη, Καταστροφή, Απάτη, και Θάνατος

findings.location: All remaining Scripture quotations and poem
findings.source_quote: Concerning Jesus of Nazareth ... through a glass, darkly ... I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.
findings.suggested_fix: Use contemporary Modern Greek throughout the remaining quotations and poem, not archaizing or pseudo-Ancient Greek. This includes Luke 24:19, 1 Corinthians 13:12, Luke 24:20, both occurrences of Luke 24:21, Genesis 15:12, 2 Corinthians 1:9, Genesis 41:1, Psalm 105:18-19, Luke 24:22-23, the Elijah quotation, John 1:29, Luke 7:19, Matthew 27:46, and all six poem lines. For example, render the poem’s last line «Σηκώθηκα, βγήκα και Σε ακολούθησα». Preserve references and line breaks; restore source em tags wherever replaced with quotation marks.
findings.translation_quote: Περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου ... διὰ κατόπτρου ἐνώπιον, ἐν αἰνίγματι ... Ἔγειρα, ἐξῆλθον, καὶ Σὲ ἠκολούθησα.
